name: Stratum MagLine Transit Operator Night Rig
description: A complete night-shift transit operator's uniform built for the underground MagLine corridors of GLMZ. The foundation is a charcoal-grey moisture-wicking synth-wool pullover with a reinforced collar and a Stratum Logistics embroidered patch at the left breast, worn under a navy insulated vest with hi-vis orange paneling across the shoulders and a reflective Stratum logo strip running vertically down the back. The vest features a rear channel seam for basic spinal rig accommodation and two deep cargo pockets with magnetic closures. Matching straight-leg transit trousers in the same charcoal synth-wool have reinforced knee panels, a wide tool loop at the right thigh, and an elasticated waistband that accommodates tail geneware through a rear adjustable vent. A navy knit beanie with a woven hi-vis stripe across the brow sits low over the ears. On the feet, matte black steel-toe platform boots with oil-resistant outsoles and side-zip closures for fast donning complete the kit, with reflective piping along the heel. The whole rig reads clean, institutional, slightly tired.
functionality: Spinal rig rear channel seam, tail-vent adjustable waistband, reflective safety paneling for low-light tunnel environments, magnetic cargo pocket closures, steel-toe footwear, tool loop, moisture-wicking base layer for temperature regulation in climate-variable underground corridors.
what_it_says: You clock in and you clock out. You know the tunnels by feel. You've worn this uniform long enough that the patches have patches, and you still iron the collar because it costs you nothing and it's the only thing you control on shift. Loyal, institutional, quietly dignified.
worn_by: shift supervisors on the night run
story_hooks: A transit operator wearing this uniform witnesses something in the tunnel that Stratum Logistics officially says never happened — and the embroidered name patch on the chest makes them very easy to identify.

The reflective strips on the vest are not just safety equipment — a runner tells the party they can be used to signal contacts in specific MagLine stations using a code the operators developed themselves.
An NPC in this uniform approaches the players during a night shift changeover, speaking quietly: they've been running contraband in the cargo vest pockets for six months and someone finally noticed.

physical_description.visual_profile: A utilitarian transit worker's uniform exuding institutional authority and underground practicality. The silhouette is functional and grounded—straight lines, accessible pockets, and visibility-first design. On-body, it reads as purposeful and worn-in, neither flashy nor entirely colorless. The hi-vis orange cuts through the charcoal and navy like emergency lighting in a tunnel.
physical_description.fit: Straight and accommodating. The pullover sits relaxed at the torso for unrestricted movement in tight MagLine cabins. The vest drapes without bunching. Trousers are straight-leg with a high waistband, designed for long shifts and augmentation tolerance—no cinching or compression except at reinforced knee panels. Boots are chunky and grounded.
physical_description.primary_material: Charcoal synth-wool (pullover and trousers)—moisture-wicking, durable, institution-grade. Navy insulated vest shell in treated ballistic weave. Knit beanie in acrylic blend. Matte black steel-reinforced leather and synthetic composite on boots.
physical_description.texture: The synth-wool has a subtle nap—practical, low-sheen, slightly fuzzy to the touch. Vest shell is rigid and windproof with a slight crinkle. Beanie knit is tight and warm. Boot leather is heavily treated and scuffed from repeated wear, with visible micro-scratches from the platform.
physical_description.color_scheme: Charcoal grey base (pullover, trousers), navy insulated vest, hi-vis orange horizontal shoulder panels and beanie stripe, matte black boots. Reflective piping in silver-grey accent. Stratum Logistics branding in white stitched embroidery and woven tags.
physical_description.closures: Pullover is simple crew-neck pullover. Vest features magnetic snap closures across the front (quiet, reliable in cold). Trousers have a standard elasticated waistband with adjustable rear vent for geneware accommodation. Boot side-zips with friction-fit tabs for one-handed fastening. Cargo pockets on vest use magnetic snaps.
distinctive_features: Stratum Logistics embroidered patch at left breast—faded slightly from washing
Vertical reflective logo strip running down back of vest for visibility in tunnel lighting
Rear channel seam in vest for basic spinal rig pass-through
Reinforced knee panels on trousers—visible darker grey patch stitching
Wide tool loop at right thigh with faint wear marks from repeated use
Elasticated rear vent on trousers with adjustable toggle for tail geneware
Woven hi-vis stripe across beanie brow—slightly loose from wash cycles
Reflective heel piping on boots—scuffed silver
Oil-resistant boot outsoles with visible tread wear and dark staining
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 3 (working class, corporation-issued). Clean and functional but not customized. Uniform standardization signals mid-tier logistics employment.
physical_description.cultural_context: This is the uniform of GLMZ's MagLine—the underground transit spine connecting the GLMZ. Wearing it signals reliable infrastructure work, night-shift commitment, and corpo-sanctioned reliability. The wearer is blue-collar but not sub-grade, trusted with critical systems. A uniform like this suggests someone with geneware (tail, likely), probably augmented with at least a basic spinal rig. Not flashy, not rebellious—just the clothes of someone moving people and cargo through the dark.
physical_description.condition_typical: Worn-in and institutional. The uniform is clean—Stratum demands that—but shows honest use. The embroidered patch has slight fraying at the edges from repeated laundering. The knee panels are darker from both wear and age. The beanie stripe is slightly loose. The boots have visible scuffs and the heel piping is dull. Nothing broken, everything functional. This is what Day 1500 of a uniform looks like.
